en lejebolig.explanation: "En lejebolig" means "a rental home". It is built from "at leje" (to rent) and "en bolig" (a home). To say you want to find one, say: "Jeg leder efter en lejebolig" (I am looking for a rental home).

en lejekontrakt.explanation: "En lejekontrakt" means "a lease". It is built from "at leje" (to rent) and "en kontrakt" (a contract). The word "kontrakt" also appears in "en arbejdskontrakt" (a work contract).

en lejer.explanation: "En lejer" means "a tenant". It comes from the verb "at leje" (to rent). The other side is "en udlejer" (a landlord), the person who rents out a home: "Vores udlejer er flink" (Our landlord is nice).

en lejlighed.explanation: "En lejlighed" means "an apartment". To say you rent one, say: "Vi lejer en lejlighed i København" (We are renting an apartment in Copenhagen). A different meaning is a chance or occasion: "Jeg ringer til dig ved lejlighed" (I will call you when I get the chance).

en lejr.explanation: "En lejr" means "a camp". To say a class goes to camp, say: "Klassen tager på lejr" (The class goes to camp). To say people set up a camp, use "at slå lejr" (to pitch camp): "De slog lejr ved søen" (They pitched camp by the lake).

en lejrskole.explanation: "En lejrskole" means "a school camp trip". It is built from "en lejr" (a camp) and "en skole" (a school). To say a class goes on one, leave out "en": "Vi tager på lejrskole" (We are going on a school camp trip).

en lektion.explanation: "En lektion" means "a lesson". To say which subject, add "i" (in): "Vi har en lektion i engelsk" (We have a lesson in English). Do not mix it up with "lektier" (homework): "Jeg laver lektier" (I do homework).

en leopard.explanation: "En leopard" means "a leopard". To say what its coat looks like, use "pletter" (spots): "En leopard har pletter" (A leopard has spots).

en letbane.explanation: "En letbane" means "a light rail". It is built from "let" (light) and "en bane" (a track). In Denmark, there are light rail lines in the cities of Aarhus and Odense.

en lever.explanation: "En lever" means "a liver". In Denmark, "leverpostej" (liver pate) is a common spread on bread. Do not mix it up with "at leve" (to live): "Jeg lever" (I live).

en leverandør.explanation: "En leverandør" means "a supplier". It comes from the verb "at levere" (to deliver). To say what a supplier supplies, add "af" (of): "Vi har en ny leverandør af kaffe" (We have a new supplier of coffee).

en levering.explanation: "En levering" means "a delivery". It comes from the verb "at levere" (to deliver). To say when a delivery arrives, say: "Leveringen kommer i morgen" (The delivery arrives tomorrow).

en leveringstid.explanation: "En leveringstid" means "a delivery time". It is built from "en levering" (a delivery) and "en tid" (a time). To ask how long you will wait, say: "Hvad er leveringstiden?" (What is the delivery time?) Do not mix it up with "en leveringsdato" (a delivery date), which is one fixed day: "Leveringsdatoen er den fjerde" (The delivery date is the fourth).

en lidelse.explanation: "En lidelse" means "a suffering / a disorder". It comes from the verb "at lide" (to suffer). To say people went through a great deal of pain, use the meaning "suffering": "Der var megen lidelse i krigen" (There was much suffering in the war).

en lift.explanation: "En lift" means "a ride", as in being driven in someone's car. To ask for one, say: "Kan jeg få en lift?" (Can I get a ride?) To offer one, say: "Jeg giver dig en lift" (I will give you a ride).

en liga.explanation: "En liga" means "a league". In Denmark, the top soccer league is called "Superligaen" (the Super League). To say a team is in the league, use "i" (in): "Holdet spiller i ligaen" (The team plays in the league).

en ligevægt.explanation: "En ligevægt" means "an equilibrium". It is built from "lige" (equal) and "en vægt" (a weight). To say someone loses their balance, say: "Han mistede ligevægten" (He lost his balance).

en lighed.explanation: "En lighed" means "a similarity". A very common phrase is "ligheder og forskelle" (similarities and differences): "Vi ser på ligheder og forskelle" (We look at similarities and differences). A different meaning is equality: "lighed for loven" (equality before the law).

en lighter.explanation: "En lighter" means "a lighter". To ask someone for one, say: "Har du en lighter?" (Do you have a lighter?)

en ligning.explanation: "En ligning" means "an equation". To say you work one out, use "at løse" (to solve): "Jeg løser en ligning" (I solve an equation).

en lillebror.explanation: "En lillebror" means "a little brother". It is built from "lille" (little) and "en bror" (a brother). He stays your "lillebror" when he is grown up. To ask about him, say: "Hvad hedder din lillebror?" (What is your little brother called?)

en lillesøster.explanation: "En lillesøster" means "a little sister". It is built from "lille" (little) and "en søster" (a sister). She stays your "lillesøster" when she is grown up. To ask about her, say: "Hvad hedder din lillesøster?" (What is your little sister called?)

en lime.explanation: "En lime" means "a lime". To ask for lime in a drink, say: "Vand med lime, tak" (Water with lime, please).

en lineal.explanation: "En lineal" means "a ruler", as in the measuring tool. To say the other meaning, a person who rules a country, use "en hersker" (a sovereign): "Kongen var en mægtig hersker" (The king was a powerful ruler).

en linje.explanation: "En linje" means "a line". To say a bus or train route, use it with a number: "Tag linje 5" (Take line 5). For people waiting in a line, use "en kø" (a queue): "Der er en lang kø" (There is a long queue).
